questions: What is the exact definition of "splitting A at one position into two subarrays" - does it mean we choose an index i and split into (A_1,...,A_i) and (A_{i+1},...,A_N)?
Is the constraint 1 ≤ i ≤ N-1 inclusive of both endpoints, meaning we must have at least one element in each subarray?
When counting distinct integers, does each subarray's count include all unique values that appear at least once in that subarray?
What should be the output format - is it just a single integer representing the maximum sum?
Are duplicate values in the sequence handled correctly by counting each distinct value only once per subarray?
Is the input guaranteed to have at least 2 elements given the constraint N ≥ 2?
Should we consider all possible split positions from i=1 to i=N-1 and return the maximum among all of them?
What is the expected behavior when the sequence contains the same element repeated throughout - does it still count as one distinct element per subarray?

inline_prompts:
This problem is a simplified version of Problem F.
You are given an integer sequence of length N: A = (A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_N).
When splitting A at one position into two subarrays, find the maximum possible sum of the counts of distinct integers in those subarrays.
More formally, find the maximum sum of the following two values for an integer i such that 1 \leq i \leq N-1: the count of distinct integers in (A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_i), and the count of distinct integers in (A_{i+1}, A_{i+2}, \ldots, A_N), They must be contiguous and non-empty subarrays obtained by splitting A at one position.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N
A_1 A_2 \ldots A_N
Output
Print the answer.
Constraints
- 2 \leq N \leq 3 \times 10^5
- 1 \leq A_i \leq N (1 \leq i \leq N)
- All input values are integers.
